explain: An RTI is a letter that asks a government office for information it holds. The office must answer within 30 days.
explainLetters: We have {n, plural, one {# ready-made letter} other {# ready-made letters}} for {district}: pick a topic, copy the letter and send it.
explainOwn: Pick “Write my own letter”, fill in your questions and send it. The steps are below.
tileBplSub: Attach a copy of your BPL card
pickTitle: What do you want to know?
pickHint: Tap a topic. Each one is a ready letter to the right office.
ownSub: Your question is not in the list? Use a blank letter.
ownHow: Copy this letter, then write the office's name and your questions in the empty places. Ask for papers or facts, not opinions, and keep each question short.
ownLetter:
To
The Public Information Officer (PIO)
[Name and address of the office]

Subject: Request for information under the Right to Information Act, 2005

Sir or Madam,

Please give me the following information:
1. [Your first question]
2. [Your second question]

I have paid the application fee of ₹[amount] by [postal order / demand draft / cash receipt number].
(If you are below the poverty line: I am below the poverty line; a copy of my BPL card is attached, so no fee is due.)

Name:
Address:
Phone:
Date:
Signature:
postWho: Works for every office, and is the usual way for state and district offices.
post1: Print or write the letter, and sign it.
post2: Add the fee in the way the office accepts it: usually a postal order, a demand draft, or cash against a receipt.
post2Fee: Add the {fee} fee in the way the office accepts it: usually a postal order, a demand draft, or cash against a receipt.
post3: Send it by registered post or Speed Post to the PIO, or hand it in and ask for a receipt.
post4: Keep a copy of the letter and the receipt. You will need them for an appeal.
onlineWho: RTI Online is for central government offices. Some states have their own RTI website; the Information Commission's website will say.
bplNote: Below the poverty line? You pay no fee: attach a copy of your BPL card instead.
timelineSimple: The RTI Act, 2005 gives every step a time limit. If a limit passes, you can move to the next step.
tl1Body: To the Public Information Officer (PIO) of the office, with the fee.
tl2Body: The PIO must reply within 30 days, or within 48 hours when a person's life or liberty is at stake.
tl3Body: No reply, or not happy with it? Appeal to the First Appellate Authority, a senior officer in the same office.
tl4Body: Still no answer? Appeal to the {commission}, or to the Central Information Commission for central government offices.
sentOnHint: Pick the date to see when the reply is due. We do not save or send this date.
appealBy: No reply by then? You can file the first appeal until {date}.
